value: write-scan-for-single-writer (cast and withdrawn the same day — its premise was falsified within the hour by the ruling below; see `why`)

Recorded here so they are not mistaken for scheduled. (1) PER-INTENTION WRITE-THROUGH — 'those intentions could all update that folder rather than launching the compiler for it': sanctioned, unbuilt. Today every refresh is a whole-folder copy. This ticket makes such a writer CHECKABLE (its output either matches the source or it does not) but does not add one. (2) THE EVENING RUN — 'supposed to run each evening, assuming that we've sorted who that belongs to so that device can launch it': the ownership is explicitly unsorted and that is Akien's to settle. Worth putting in front of him when it comes up: compile-on-read already exists and fires (recompile_gate.sh, poked by /intent before it consults the folder), so the evening run's real job is the case a read never covers — a source that changed and that nobody has since consulted, and deletions. That is a smaller job than 'keep it fresh', and it may be that verify_lab reporting drift is the more useful evening act than a copy that silently erases it.
